summary: JavassistProxyFactoryTest.testGetInvoker is order-dependent: it passes alone but fails when it runs after RpcContextTest.testAsync, which leaves a started AsyncContext in the thread-local RpcContext.
root_cause: RpcContext is held in an InternalThreadLocal and is cleared only by RpcContext.removeContext(). RpcContextTest.testAsync installs an AsyncContext, calls RpcContext.startAsync(), and never removes the context; it even asserts that isAsyncStarted() is still true after stopAsync(), so the started state survives the test. In the observed ordered execution, the subsequent test inherits the same thread-local context. AbstractProxyInvoker.invoke consults RpcContext.getContext(): because isAsyncStarted() is true it takes the branch that returns new AsyncRpcResult(rpcContext.getAsyncContext().getInternalFuture()) instead of new RpcResult(obj). The returned Result is therefore derived from the future the polluter already completed rather than from this invocation's own return value, so the assertion comparing the invoker's value against origin.echo("aa") no longer sees "aa". The victim's own code is correct; the failure exists only for orders in which the polluter runs first.
recommended_action: Make RpcContextTest.testAsync restore thread state before it finishes, for example by calling RpcContext.removeContext() in an @After method or at the end of the test, so no started AsyncContext leaks into subsequently executed tests on the same thread.
